dimensions.name: past work
dimensions.evidence: Technical lead on AI trip planner at KKday; owned agent design, core backend, and Android stream reader; explained latency trade-off (streaming vs. gating final itinerary); described a hard duplicate-day bug with root cause (client reconnect without last-day), fix (track last day, requestId), and production measurement (duplicate count zero, reconnect rate stable); gave a delivery risk example at Debon Securities with options, PM decision, and personal follow-up.

dimensions.name: current ability
dimensions.evidence: Designed a mobile wallet with clear client/server/local storage ownership; used Long cents, client transfer ID, local intent persistence, idempotent retries, four result states (success, clear failure, processing, unknown); correctly handled lost response with process kill via lookup by client ID; handled concurrent transfers with conditional updates; prevented cross-account data leak with account/session tagging; integrated chat-initiated payment with native confirmation and server binding to payer, recipient, amount, expiry.

dimensions.name: handling unknowns
dimensions.evidence: Asked clarifying questions before design (balance custody, currencies, offline behavior); adapted to new conditions (chat entry, stream disconnect, idempotency window expiry, two Alex contacts, recipient change after confirm); explained what the binding stops and what it cannot stop (user picking wrong Alex); proposed reconciliation for expired idempotency window; identified escalation signals (pending count growing after pause, ledger debit without matching record).

dimensions.name: shipping product
dimensions.evidence: Scoped two-week first version (balance, transfer, history, native confirm, pending/unknown states); identified sign-off owners (tech lead, product owner, risk/compliance); listed pre-release tests (lost response with process kill, replay, concurrent transfers, account switch); proposed incident response (pause submissions, keep reads, cap pending per account, find cause, resume in stages); defined resume criteria (pending flat or falling for an hour, backend owner confirms stuck transfers, reconciliation owner signs off).

strongest: current ability: wallet design with idempotency, local intent persistence, and correct handling of lost responses, concurrent transfers, and account switching.
risks: Production evidence for the duplicate-day fix is limited to logged sessions and manual replay; no broader device/network coverage.
Incident response plan is solid but lacks concrete monitoring thresholds or dashboards beyond pending count and crash rate.
Some answers repeated points (e.g., native confirm binding, client ID reuse) without adding new depth, suggesting occasional redundancy rather than deeper trade-off analysis.
